ask: The company's registration or license number, and its class
Any job-size limit the license has
General liability insurance; workers' comp where the business has employees
A bond, where the state's form asks for one
pf.license.holder: The business; plus a qualifying person where the state's form names one. Waterproofing and sump crews hold their own license where the state's form asks; a structural engineer holds their own license where a plan must be stamped; an electrician wires the sump pump where the rules require it.
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
blocks: No foundation work goes live until the company's registration or license checks out, where one is required
A job over the license's size limit is never offered or quoted: the owner is told why
pf.license.renewals: License, insurance and bond dates kept; reminded 30 days out; a lapse pauses new bookings
pf.license.design_studio: A consult at the office needs no license in most states. The work it leads to is booked under the contractor license.
pf.license.background: Background checks only where the state's form asks

pf.services.capacity: One estimator or advisor per booking; one install crew per job; the office's desk is saved with long sessions
pf.services.skills: Estimates and running a job: crew leads. Plan consults: plan advisors. Piers, anchors and drains: install crews. Stamped plans: a structural engineer. Wiring: a licensed electrician.
pf.services.nobody_home: Estimates and small jobs: nobody needs to be home if the basement is reachable. Work days: an adult on the booking is reachable by phone.
pf.services.online: A plan consult can be a video or phone call (counts as at the office)
pf.services.smallest_job: A switch the owner sets: the smallest job taken, with smaller requests pointed elsewhere (the example takes no repair under $1,500 and sends smaller ones to the list jobs).

before_times: What is the problem? (a crack, a bowing wall, a sloping floor, water coming in)
Where in the home, and about how long is it
When did you first see it, and has it changed
The year the home was built, and the kind of foundation if you know it
after_time: Who will sign the contract? Everyone on the deed should be at the estimate visit
Do you own the home or rent? (the owner must sign)
Access to the basement or crawl space, and where machines can reach outside
Sprinkler lines, drains or utility lines near the wall
Pets at home during the work
pf.questions.who_may_book: An adult who owns the property, or someone with the owner's written OK. A renter's job needs the owner to sign.
studio: Which area, and a rough budget (on the secure page)

stop.words: gas smell, hissing near a gas line, sparking or smoking wires, a carbon monoxide alarm
stop.says: Leave the house now. Then call 911 and the gas or power company.
stop.booking: no booking; a new request must say the home was made safe

stop.words: a wall or floor giving way right now, a loud crack with movement, a ceiling sagging or falling
stop.says: Get everyone out of that room, and call 911 if anyone is at risk.

steps_then_go_on.words: water coming into the basement or near outlets
steps_then_go_on.says: Stay out of the water and away from the outlets. Don't touch wiring or the sump pump. Call an electrician first.

steps_then_go_on.words: a wall bowing in, or a new wide crack
steps_then_go_on.says: Keep people and things away from that wall, and don't stack anything against it. We'll look at it first.

pf.safety.business_line: Questions about whether a wall is safe to stay near, about a neighbor's wall or about a septic system go to the business's own line

pf.first_steps.before_quote: The estimate visit at the property, with everyone who will sign there
after_contract: The cancel window ends before any work or orders, where the state's rules give one
The utility locate: the crew asks for buried lines to be marked before anyone digs, and the marks stay until the work is done
The permit, pulled by the license holder in the business's name, where the work needs one; a structural engineer's stamped plan where the rules require it
Piers, anchors and materials ordered once the window ends
prep: Clear the wall and the floor in front of it, and move boxes and shelves away
Keep pets and everyone else out of the work area
Mark sprinkler heads and lines you know about
Put any gate or lockbox code on the secure page
Don't stack anything against a cracked wall
studio_prep: Bring photos and rough measurements of the area
Bring any samples or colors you already like

pf.visit.check_in: Estimate visit: the check-in code at the door. Each work day: that day's code, or the lockbox and a start photo when nobody is home. Office: the code at the desk.
pf.visit.at_the_visit: The estimator looks at the wall, floor and drainage, measures the cracks and the slope, photographs and notes the water paths; the written quote follows within 3 business days, good for 30 days
pf.visit.changes: A written change order, priced and signed by both, before any changed work. A rotted sill plate, more piers than the quote has, a buried tank or old pipe wrap found are priced this way.
pf.visit.outside_checks: An engineer's check of the piers and a permit inspection, where the permit requires them
pf.visit.done: The engineer's or permit check where needed, then the walk-through and punch list, then DONE on the last work day; the care notes go with it
pf.visit.studio_done: DONE after the consult, with the plan advisor's notes and the picks saved for the estimate
pf.visit.before_photos: The wall, the cracks (with a ruler), the floor, the drains and anything already damaged

pf.money.estimate: The example's $89 estimate visit is credited to the job; billed only if no contract follows. A free estimate is the safe start.
pf.money.no_money_before_contract: On project work, nothing is taken before the contract is signed by everyone on the deed
pf.money.deposit: Only after signing; the deposit cap comes from the state's form
pf.money.kept_apart: Money paid before the work is kept apart or bonded where the state's rules require it (a switch from the state's form)
pf.money.stages: Each stage is billed only when it's done and any check has passed: the start, the piers or anchors in and the wall checked, the finish. Never ahead of the work
pf.money.last_payment: After the walk-through and any engineer's or permit check
pf.money.change_orders: Added to the next stage bill
pf.money.big_bills: Bank transfer through the company's own Stripe, for bills over the owner's amount (the example: $500); paid once it clears. A check also works: the crew lead texts 'paid check'.
pf.money.tax: Tax on materials and labor follows the state's form
pf.money.studio: The waterproofing plan session's $55 is credited to the job if Alex signs; the $20 missed-consult fee only after Sam OKs it

never_in_texts: Contract, change order and permit papers (secure page only, with a copy by email)
pf.messages.minors: Never booked by a minor; a child at home is never the one who lets the crew in

pf.staff.roles: Crew leads (Abel, Vera): estimates, quotes and running the job, with the crew. Plan advisors (Remy, Odette) at the office.
pf.staff.licenses: The company holds the contractor registration or license. Where the state's form also licenses each person, each one may add a number (optional, shown as given, not checked by Rosie). Subcontractors hold their own, as the business says.
pf.staff.who_oks: Sam OKs quotes and change orders over $500; Pat may OK them too, and Sam's answer wins
pf.staff.stand_in: Another crew lead may take an estimate visit; a job keeps its crew lead unless Sam moves it

pf.rules.contract: A written contract for project work where the state's rules require one, signed by everyone on the deed and by the business before any money
pf.rules.contract_parts: The parts the state's form lists (license number, dates, price, deposit, cancel notice, any lien notice)
pf.rules.cancel_window: A cancel window after signing, where the state's rules give one; work and orders wait for it
pf.rules.permits: Pulled by the license holder in the business's name, never the homeowner's
pf.rules.change_orders: Written and signed by both before the changed work
pf.rules.final: The engineer's or permit sign-off where needed, before the last payment
pf.rules.lien_waivers: Lien waivers from the business and its subcontractors with the last payment, where the state's rules provide them
pf.rules.show: The license number on the listing, the quote, the contract and the receipt, where the state's rules require it
pf.rules.warranty: 1 year on workmanship (the example's); the maker's warranty on piers and anchors, as the quote says; cracks may reappear, and the contract says what is covered

pf.edges.weather: Heavy rain or frozen ground on a dig day: the work moves, with no fee; the crew lead checks the forecast the day before
pf.edges.engineer_plan: The engineer's plan needs more than the quote has: a change order first, and the start may move
pf.edges.line_in_the_way: A marked utility line is in the way: the crew plans around it and digs by hand near it; the start may move a day or two
pf.edges.hidden_conditions: A rotted sill plate, rot or old pipe wrap found when the wall is opened: a change order before the fix; old pipe wrap that may contain asbestos stops that part of the work
pf.edges.moving_wall: A wall that keeps moving, or a crack that grows during the work: the crew lead stops, tells Sam and Alex in writing, and the engineer is asked
pf.edges.water_in: Water coming in during the work: the crew pumps, protects the floor and the outlets, and tells Alex
pf.edges.neighbor_line: Work near a property line or a neighbor's wall: the crew lead calls Alex first; a neighbor's OK is the customer's to get
pf.edges.landscaping: Plants, sod and paving moved for a dig are put back as the quote says; a larger restoration is a change order
pf.edges.permit_late: The start moves with no fee; Alex is told
pf.edges.inspection_fails: The crew fixes it and it's checked again; the next stage and its bill wait
pf.edges.cancel_after_window: Sam and the customer settle it; Rosie moves no money on its own
pf.edges.nobody_home: Estimates and small jobs with the basement reachable, with start and end photos
pf.edges.over_license_limit: Not offered, and the owner is told why
pf.edges.walk_through_dispute: Goes to Sam; the last bill waits
pf.edges.other: All other edge cases are handled the generic way

notes:
Started from contractor (pattern: project, refitted Tue Oct 27 on the frozen master): an estimate visit, a written quote, then a contract and stage bills. Facts, switches, settings and money paths are the parent's, re-worded for this work: documents, stages, photos, extrawork, firststeps, multiday, banktransfer, video; switch cancelright in flow B only (work sold at the customer's place); arrive A a set start, B a 2-hour window; cutoff 24 hours before.
Flow B main path visit|none|bill: the booking is the $89 estimate visit, credited to the job; Abel's written quote; the contract signed by everyone on the deed; $960 to start, $5,760 when the piers or anchors are in and the wall is checked, $2,880 at the finish (a $9,600 foundation repair job). The $89 keeps the master's numbers true (97 master steps hard-code it); a free estimate is the owner's choice (pf.money).
B money paths: visit|none|bill, visit|none|own, visit|card|bill, photos|deposit|bill (Crack injection, one crack, $640 from photos, a $160 deposit and $480 after). Left out: list paths. Downspout extensions ($179) and Sump pump check ($150) are in pf.services, but the master's booking cards name one list service, so a list path would show the wrong name (MASTER R02/R08).
Flow A is Sam's second company, Lee Plan Office, Lee Plan Office, a basement plan office (the master's Lee's Barbershop). Main path list|card|counter: a $35 plan consult with Remy, a card saved for the $20 missed-consult fee, paid at the office desk. The other three: list|none|counter, list|full|none (waterproofing plan session, $55, credited to the job if Alex signs), list|deposit|counter (basement repair plan, $140, $40 deposit and $100 after the visit). Video or phone plan consults are on (fact `video`): the owner's photos of the cracks and the basement are enough to talk through a plan, so the A4-01 video branch is on.
Own steps: A8-x01 (the plan consult offers the estimate visit at home), B8-x06 to B8-x08 (the permit, the utility locate and, where required, the engineer's plan go first; a late permit moves the start with no fee; an engineer who wants more piers means a change order and a possible new start) and B8-x11 / B8-x12 (a rotted sill plate found when the wall is opened: a change order first, signed by both).
Foundation work is structural: a wall or floor giving way right now, a loud crack with movement, or a ceiling falling is a stop (pf.safety), while a bowing wall or a new wide crack is safety steps and then the booking goes on, marked urgent; a crack is an everyday word here, so it is not a stop word. Digging waits for the utility locate (B8-x06), a structural engineer's stamped plan comes first where the rules require it (pf.first_steps, B8-x08), and old pipe wrap that may contain asbestos stops that part of the work (B8-30). Water in the basement near outlets is a go-on word with the safety steps, in the Spanish call (B3-11, B3-18) and in the gets-worse step (B7-17).
Booking choices: B timing settime, times window; A times setstart. Nothing is sent now: the S2-30 'Yes' branch is off, no `sentnow` fact, and the two rows that spoke of it say so (S2-30's example sentence and S1-21's 'Jobs sent now' row now read that every job is booked ahead). I searched the joined text of all eight paths for the opposite claim: only the master's own conditional lines remain ('A job sent now reads ...' in B6-13, S13-32), hidden branches aside.
Dates (not the parent's): the own steps run forward from the cancel window (ends Tue Oct 27) to the first work day Mon Nov 2: the permit to-do is Wed Oct 28 'due before the first work day, Mon Nov 2'; a late permit Fri Oct 30 with new starts Mon Nov 9 / Mon Nov 16; the trade's surprise at the lab or locate Thu Oct 29; the change order on a work day, Tue Nov 3.
Test results, health and money details stay off texts: the lab or test result is 'on your secure page' in every text (B8-x08), and special care needs at home are asked only on the secure page (pf.questions secure_page_only).
Plug-in splits kept whole (splitsKept): A7-15; B5-34, B7-55, B8-58, B8-69 (as the parent).
Names: Abel and Vera are the crew leads (the master's Jordan and Casey), Remy and Odette the plan advisors (Riley and Avery). None of them is a master customer's name. Addresses: 340 Mason Rd (the company), 17 Depot Sq (the office), 52 Cedar Ln (Alex). License numbers use an obviously fake format (FR-1042, WP-2210, PO-3305; people FR-10552, WP-10417). No state, city or law is named.
Every state rule is a switch from the state's form: the license and its job-size limit, the written contract and its parts, the deposit cap, money kept apart, the cancel window, permits, lien waivers, what must be shown.
keep: color (the master's protected-classes line in S13-40 says 'race, color, religion or sex'), pipe, valve and leak (this trade's own words), the estimate visit, roofing (the work it doesn't do).
Rename: the contractor's pairs re-worded for this work (master sentences first, then phrases, then single words); the barbershop's 'cut' and 'hair' words and its price-board words are turned into this work's words (S1-38, S1-60, S13-55, B8-34); the A3-22 / A3-23 lines that said the plug-in has no danger words now name this work's.
